mainTopic: The עגלה ערופה ceremony and the great importance of לויה, escorting travelers
overview: This amud finishes explaining the משנה about the עגלה ערופה. First a ברייתא shows that איתן means 'hard', and אחרים say it means 'old'. The heifer is killed from behind, learned from the word עריפה by the bird חטאת העוף. רבי יאשיה and רבי יונתן argue whether the valley must never have been worked in the past. רבא says both agree it may not be worked from then on. A ברייתא teaches that only work on the ground itself is forbidden there, so combing flax and cutting stones are allowed. The זקנים wash over the spot where the neck was broken. Their declaration 'our hands did not spill this blood' means they did not send the traveler off without food or לויה. This opens a long section on לויה: its endless reward (the man of לוז, פרעה and אברהם), how far each person must escort, stories of אמוראים escorting their teachers, and רבי מאיר's warning that not escorting is like spilling blood. The proof is the story of אלישע and the youths, and the גמרא explains the youths' taunt, the words 'young lads', and what אלישע 'saw', ending with the two bears.

steps.title: Verses showing that איתן means hard
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings פסוקים where איתן describes rock and mountains, which shows it means something hard.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Firm is your dwelling-place, and your nest is set in the rock.' And another פסוק says: 'Hear, O mountains, the Lord's controversy, and the enduring rocks, the foundations of the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing its proof that the word איתן means 'hard'. It does this by pointing to פסוקים where איתן goes together with rock and mountains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the עגלה ערופה is brought to a נחל איתן, so we need to know what איתן means. In both פסוקים, איתן appears next to rocks and mountains. That shows the word describes something hard and strong.

keyTerms.meaning: Strong, firm, or hard (the word being defined)
'And it says': brings another פסוק as further proof

phrases.english: "Firm is your dwelling-place, and your nest is set in the rock"
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:21

phrases.english: and it says:
"Hear, O mountains, the Lord's controversy,
and the enduring rocks, the foundations of the earth"
phrases.notes: מיכה 6:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section, which asked how we know איתן means hard
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 24:21 and מיכה 6:2, where איתן is paired with rock and mountains

steps.title: Another view: איתן means old
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say איתן means old, and they prove it from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: How do we know that איתן means old? Because it says: 'It is an ancient nation, a nation from of old.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second group, called אחרים, gives a different meaning for איתן: old. They bring their own פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, 'גוי איתן' is placed right next to 'גוי מעולם', a nation from long ago. Because the two halves match, איתן must mean ancient. So this view defines the word differently from the first view.

phrases.english: Others say:
From where do we know that "eitan" means old?
As it is stated:
"It is an ancient nation, a nation from of old"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 5:15

steps.whatToRemember: There are two meanings of איתן: hard (the first view) and old (אחרים).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different definition of the same word
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 5:15, where גוי איתן is paired with גוי מעולם

steps.title: Why is the heifer killed from behind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about breaking the heifer's neck from behind and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they break its neck with a cleaver from behind.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why the killing must be done from the back of the neck. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה only says the heifer gets עריפה. It does not say from which side. The גמרא wants to know how we know it must be done from behind.

keyTerms.meaning: They break the neck (from עֹרֶף, the back of the neck)
A cleaver, a heavy chopping knife

phrases.english: "And they break its neck with a cleaver from behind."
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that עריפה of the heifer is done from behind

steps.title: Learned from the bird sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The word עריפה is linked to the bird חטאת העוף, which is done from the back of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns 'arifa' 'arifa' from the bird sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we compare the heifer to the bird חטאת העוף, because the same word appears with both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the bird חטאת העוף, the תורה says the head is pinched 'ממול ערפו', from the back of its neck. Because the same word appears with the עגלה ערופה, this גזירה שוה teaches that the heifer is also killed from behind.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns (derives one case from another)
Breaking the neck from the back
A bird brought as a sin-offering

phrases.english: He learns "arifa" "arifa"
from the bird sin-offering.
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 5:8 the bird's head is pinched 'from the back of its neck' (ערפו). The shared word links the two cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of the word עריפה from חטאת העוף, which is done from the back of the neck

steps.title: Dispute: past or future?
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's rule that the place may not be worked, a ברייתא brings a מחלוקת: רבי יאשיה says the פסוק refers to the past, and רבי יונתן says it refers to the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And its place is forbidden to be sown or worked.' The Rabbis taught: 'Which may not be worked nor sown' refers to the past, says רבי יאשיה. רבי יונתן says: it refers to the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about the valley and brings a ברייתא where two תנאים argue about what the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יאשיה, the valley must be one that was never worked before. According to רבי יונתן, the פסוק means that after the heifer is killed there, nobody may work the land from then on. The same words are read in two different time frames.

keyTerms.meaning: Worked (the land being plowed or farmed)

phrases.english: "And its place is forbidden to be sown or worked."
The Rabbis taught:
"Which may be neither worked nor sown"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

phrases.english: refers to the past; these are the words of Rabbi Yoshiya.
phrases.notes: He means the valley must be one that was never worked or sown before.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan says: it refers to the future.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יאשיה: the place must not have been worked in the past. רבי יונתן: the place is forbidden to be worked in the future.

steps.title: רבא: everyone agrees about the future
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides agree the land is forbidden from now on. They only argue about whether past work disqualifies it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: About the future, everyone agrees, because it is written 'and shall not be sown'. Where they disagree is about the past.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא redefines the מחלוקת so that it is narrower than it first looked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ולא יזרע' is clearly in the future tense, so nobody can argue that sowing later is allowed. The only real argument is whether the valley also needs to be unworked from before. So רבי יאשיה actually holds both the past and the future rules, and רבי יונתן holds only the future rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יאשיה allows working the land in the future. According to רבא, he agrees to that and adds a requirement about the past.

phrases.english: Rava said:
About the future, everyone agrees,
as it is written: "nor sown",
where they disagree is about the past.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: לְהַבָּא — דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא's dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone forbids working the land in the future. The dispute is only about past work.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה's reading of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה argues that the פסוק did not use a clear future form, so it also teaches about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יאשיה holds: Is it written 'and shall not be worked'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יאשיה reads a past requirement into the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה meant only the future, it could have used the clear future-command form 'יעובד'. Instead it wrote 'יֵעָבֵד', which can also describe land that has not been worked. So רבי יאשיה reads it as including the past.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a rhetorical question from the wording)
Shall be worked (a clearly future form)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya holds:
Is it written "and shall not be worked"?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה סָבַר: מִי כְּתִיב ״וְלֹא יְעוּבַּד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the past dispute
steps.raayaObject: That the פסוק includes a past requirement
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verb form יֵעָבֵד rather than a clear future form

steps.title: רבי יונתן pushes back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן answers that the פסוק also did not use a clear past form.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונתן: Is it written 'which was not worked'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן turns רבי יאשיה's argument around. If the תורה meant the past, it would have used a clear past-tense word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wording was רבי יאשיה's whole proof, so רבי יונתן attacks it on the same level. The clear past form would be 'נעבד', and that is not what the פסוק says. So the wording does not prove anything about the past.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yonatan:
Is it written "which was not worked"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִי כְּתִיב ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא נֶעֱבַד״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יאשיה's proof from the wording
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יאשיה's reading of יֵעָבֵד as including the past
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A past requirement would have been written in a clear past form like נעבד

steps.title: רבי יאשיה: the word אשר points to the past
steps.stepSummary: רבי יאשיה replies that the word אשר shows the פסוק is talking about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יאשיה: 'אשר' implies the past.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה defends his view by pointing to the word אשר in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the verb is not clearly in the past, 'אשר', meaning 'which', describes the valley as it already is. So רבי יאשיה reads it as land that has not been worked until now.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoshiya:
"which" implies the past,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יונתן's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verb form alone does not show a past requirement
steps.terutzMaskana: The word אשר shows the פסוק refers to the past

steps.title: רבי יונתן: אשר comes to include something
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says אשר is a ריבוי, an extra word that adds something, and not a sign of the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונתן: 'אשר' is an amplification.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן explains how he reads the word אשר, so that it does not support רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יונתן, אשר is a ריבוי, a word that widens the פסוק, and not a sign of the past. Step 15 shows what this widening does: it stops the פסוק from being read as a narrow כלל ופרט. So both sides have now explained every word of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: An amplification: a word that comes to include something extra

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both sides forbid working the valley in the future. רבי יאשיה also requires that it was never worked before, learning this from 'אשר'. רבי יונתן reads 'אשר' as a ריבוי.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yonatan:
"which" is an amplification.
phrases.notes: Step 15 shows what this extra word does: it keeps the פסוק from being read as a narrow כלל ופרט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains away רבי יאשיה's proof from אשר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אשר seems to describe the past
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יונתן, אשר is a ריבוי, so it gives רבי יאשיה no proof that the פסוק speaks about the past.

steps.title: Combing flax and cutting stones are allowed, and all ground work is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that combing flax and cutting stones are allowed in the valley. A ברייתא then learns from the פסוק that every kind of work is forbidden there, not only sowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: it is allowed to comb flax there and to cut stones there. The Rabbis taught: from 'which may not be worked or sown' I would only know about sowing. How do I know about other kinds of work? The פסוק says 'which may not be worked,' meaning any work at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the משנה's line that some activities are allowed in the valley. Then it quotes a ברייתא showing that the words 'not be worked' forbid every kind of work, not just sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only said 'not sown,' we would think only sowing is forbidden. The words 'not be worked' are general, so they add all other kinds of work. This sets up the next question: if all work is forbidden, why mention sowing at all?

keyTerms.meaning: To comb flax, separating its fibers
The פסוק says, as a source for a teaching
In any case, meaning any kind of work at all

phrases.english: And it is permitted to comb flax there
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. 'There' means the valley where the calf was killed.

phrases.english: and to cut stones there.
The Rabbis taught:
"which may be neither worked nor sown"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:4

phrases.english: I only have sowing;
from where do we know other kinds of work?
The פסוק says: "which may not be worked"
in any way at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוּתָּר לִסְרוֹק שָׁם פִּשְׁתָּן וּלְנַקֵּר שָׁם אֲבָנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument about past work in steps 6-10 to the next line of the משנה, about which activities are allowed in the valley.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All kinds of work are forbidden in the valley, not only sowing, because the פסוק says 'not be worked.'

steps.title: Why does the פסוק also say 'not sown'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if 'not be worked' already forbids every kind of work, why does the פסוק add 'not sown'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'nor sown'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a short question that sets up its next teaching. If all work is already forbidden, the word 'sown' looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sowing is already a kind of work, so 'not be worked' should already include it. The ברייתא assumes the Torah has no wasted words, so 'not sown' must be there to teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, meaning if what was just said is true

phrases.english: If so,
why does the פסוק say "nor sown"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the specific word 'sown' is needed after step 11 showed that all work is forbidden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the extra word 'not sown' come to teach?

steps.title: Sowing shows that only work on the ground itself is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Sowing is work done on the ground itself, so only that kind of work is forbidden. Combing flax and cutting stones are not done on the ground, so they are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It tells you: just as sowing is special because it is done on the ground itself, so too anything done on the ground itself is forbidden. This leaves out combing flax and cutting stones, which are not done on the ground itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. 'Sown' is the model that shows which kind of work is forbidden, and this explains the משנה's rule from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not be worked' forbids work in general, and 'sown' narrows it to work like sowing, meaning work on the soil itself. Combing flax and cutting stones can happen in the valley without touching the ground, so they are allowed. This is the source for the משנה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too, comparing other cases to a model case
On the ground itself, the soil

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that combing flax and cutting stones are allowed in the valley.

phrases.english: To tell you: just as sowing is special
because it is done on the ground itself,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁהוּא בְּגוּפָהּ שֶׁל קַרְקַע.
phrases.english: so too anything done on the ground itself is forbidden.
This leaves out combing flax and cutting stones,
which are not done on the ground itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Sown' is the model case. It limits the forbidden work to work done on the ground itself, so combing flax and cutting stones are allowed.

steps.title: Maybe this is a כלל ופרט and only sowing is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe 'not be worked' is a כלל and 'not sown' is a פרט. Then, by the rule of כלל ופרט, only sowing would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: 'which may not be worked' is a general statement, and 'nor sown' is a detail. When there is a general statement followed by a detail, the general statement includes only what is in the detail. So sowing is forbidden, but nothing else is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by using a well-known rule for reading פסוקים. That rule would make the פסוק forbid only sowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט, a general word followed by a specific word is limited to the specific word. If that rule applied here, plowing and other work would be allowed, and only sowing would be forbidden. This directly attacks step 11, which said all ground work is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead, offering a different reading
A general statement followed by a detail; the general is limited to the detail

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the ברייתא's 'just as sowing' reading in step 13. That reading forbids all work like sowing. The כלל ופרט reading would forbid sowing alone.

phrases.english: But say: "which may not be worked" is a general statement,
and "nor sown" is a detail.
With a general statement and then a detail,
the general statement includes only what is in the detail:
sowing, yes, it is forbidden;
anything else, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the ברייתא in steps 11 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's teaching that every kind of ground work is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק has the shape of a כלל ופרט, and that rule would limit the forbidden work to sowing alone.

steps.title: The word אשר is a ריבוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word אשר adds to the meaning. Because of it, the פסוק is not read as a plain כלל ופרט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'which' is an extra word that adds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in a few words. The word אשר widens the meaning, so the narrow כלל ופרט rule does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra word that adds, a ריבוי, breaks the plain pattern of a כלל ופרט. So the general words 'not be worked' keep their wide meaning, and the ברייתא's reading stands. This uses the same idea that רבי יונתן said in step 10: אשר is a ריבוי.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra word that adds or widens what the פסוק includes

steps.whatToRemember: All work done on the ground itself is forbidden in the valley. Work like combing flax and cutting stones, which does not touch the ground, is allowed. The word אשר keeps the פסוק from being read as a narrow כלל ופרט.

phrases.english: "Which" is an extra word that adds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an extra word changes how the פסוק is read
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is a כלל ופרט, so only sowing is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the ריבוי אשר, the general words stay wide, and all ground work is forbidden.

steps.title: The זקנים wash their hands over the spot where the calf's neck was broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the זקנים wash their hands. A ברייתא learns from the extra word 'הערופה' that they wash over the exact place where the calf's neck was broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the elders of the city wash their hands. The Rabbis taught: 'And all the elders of that city, who are closest to the dead man, shall wash their hands over the calf whose neck was broken in the valley.' The פסוק did not need to say 'whose neck was broken.' So why does it say it? To teach that they wash over the place where the calf's neck was broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, about the זקנים washing their hands. A ברייתא explains where they must wash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is only one calf in this story, so 'whose neck was broken' seems extra. The ברייתא learns from this word that the washing is tied to the place where the neck was broken. So the זקנים must wash right at that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: The elders of the city, the judges of the closest town
The dead man, the person who was killed
The place where its neck was broken

phrases.english: The elders of the city wash their hands, and so on.
The Rabbis taught:
"And all the elders of that city,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:6

phrases.english: who are closest to the dead man,
shall wash their hands
over the calf whose neck was broken in the valley."
The פסוק did not need to say "whose neck was broken,"
so why does the פסוק say "whose neck was broken"?
To teach that they wash over the place where the calf's neck was broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, about the זקנים washing their hands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זקנים wash their hands over the exact place where the calf's neck was broken, which is learned from the extra word הערופה.

steps.title: Why Would the Elders Need to Say They Did Not Kill?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק has the זקנים declare 'our hands did not spill this blood.' The question is asked: would anyone really think the בית דין are murderers?
steps.simpleTranslation: The זקנים say: 'Our hands did not spill this blood, and our eyes did not see.' But would anyone really think that the judges of the court kill people?!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה quotes the declaration of the זקנים and points out that, read plainly, it seems pointless. It is setting up the real meaning, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody suspects respected judges of murder, so a statement denying it seems unneeded. That means the words must hint at something less obvious.

keyTerms.meaning: would it even enter our minds? (a question that says the idea is unthinkable)

phrases.english: "And they shall say: Our hands did not spill

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הַדָּם הַזֶּה וְעֵינֵינוּ לֹא רָאוּ״,
phrases.english: this blood, nor did our eyes see,"
phrases.notes: דברים 21:7

phrases.english: But would it ever enter our minds

steps.title: The Elders Mean They Did Not Neglect the Traveler
steps.stepSummary: The declaration means: we did not send him off without food, and we did not let him leave without לויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they mean: he did not come to us and we sent him away without food, and we did not see him and let him go off alone without anyone escorting him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the real meaning: the זקנים declare that they were not even indirectly responsible for the death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Our hands' means we did not send him away hungry. 'Our eyes' means we did not watch him leave alone without an escort. So failing to give food or לויה is treated as a kind of partial blame for a death.

keyTerms.meaning: escorting a guest or traveler on his way

steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the idea of לויה comes from. The rest of the sugya builds on it.

phrases.english: Rather: he did not come into our hands
phrases.notes: He means the traveler did not come to us for help.

phrases.english: and then we sent him off without food,
and we did not see him and leave him without accompaniment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by reading the declaration as being about neglect, not murder.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The זקנים declare that they did not leave the traveler without food or without an escort.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: People Can Be Forced to Escort
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that people may be forced to do לויה, because its reward has no limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר used to say: we force people to escort others, because the reward for escorting has no limit.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the זקנים were discussing לויה, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows how important לויה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר makes לויה something a person can be required to do, not just a nice extra. His reason is that its reward is endless. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Meir would say:
We force people to accompany others,
for the reward of accompanying has no limit,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of לויה in step 18 and opens a section on its reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People may be forced to do לויה, because its reward is unlimited.

steps.title: Proof From the Man Who Showed the City Entrance
steps.stepSummary: A man showed the army the way into the city. The whole city was destroyed, but he and his family were spared.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'The watchers saw a man leaving the city and said to him: Please show us the way into the city, and we will be kind to you.' And it says: 'He showed them the way into the city.' What kindness did they do for him? They killed the whole city by the sword, but they let that man and his family go.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר proves the huge reward for לויה from the story in שופטים: a man who helped travelers find their way was rescued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing someone the way is a small form of לויה. For that small act, the man and his whole family were saved while everyone else in the city died.

phrases.english: as it is said: "And the watchers saw
a man coming out of the city,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמְרוּ לוֹ הַרְאֵנוּ נָא אֶת מְבוֹא הָעִיר
phrases.english: and they said to him: Show us, please, the entrance of the city,
and we will deal kindly with you,"
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:24

phrases.english: and it is written: "And he showed them the entrance of the city,"
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:25

phrases.english: And what kindness did they do for him?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר הָרְגוּ לְפִי חֶרֶב,
phrases.english: That the whole city they killed by the sword,
but that man and his family they sent away free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק that supports רבי מאיר's claim in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The reward for לויה is unlimited.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 1:24-25, the man who showed the entrance and was spared with his family.

steps.title: The City of לוז Is Protected Forever
steps.stepSummary: The man built the city לוז. A ברייתא says no conqueror ever harmed it, and even מלאך המות cannot enter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it לוז; that is its name to this day.' It is taught: this is the לוז where תכלת is dyed. This is the לוז that סנחריב did not uproot and נבוכדנצר did not destroy. Even מלאך המות may not pass through it. Instead, when its elders feel they have lived long enough, they go outside the wall and die there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how far the man's reward reached. His city and his descendants were protected for all generations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward did not stop with saving the man himself. His city was spared by every conqueror, and death itself has no power inside it. This shows that the reward really is 'without limit.'

keyTerms.meaning: the blue dye used for ציצית
mixed it up, sent its people into exile
they have had enough of life

phrases.english: "And the man went to the land of the Hittites,
and he built a city and called its name Luz;
that is its name to this day,"
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:26

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: הִיא לוּז שֶׁצּוֹבְעִין בָּהּ תְּכֵלֶת,
phrases.english: It is taught: This is Luz, where they dye sky-blue wool,

phrases.aramaic: הִיא לוּז שֶׁבָּא סַנְחֵרִיב וְלֹא בִּלְבְּלָהּ,
phrases.english: this is Luz, which Sennacherib came to and did not scatter,
phrases.notes: סנחריב moved whole nations into exile, but he left this city alone.

phrases.english: Nebuchadnezzar came and did not destroy it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת אֵין לוֹ רְשׁוּת לַעֲבוֹר בָּהּ.
phrases.english: and even the angel of death has no permission to pass through it.
Rather, its elders,
when they feel they have had enough of life,
go out beyond the wall, and they die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 20 and shows that the man's reward lasted for all generations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוז, the man's city, is protected forever from conquerors and even from death.

steps.title: קל וחומר: Real לויה Earns Even More
steps.stepSummary: If the man who only pointed the way earned eternal rescue, someone who actually walks with a guest earns far more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? This Canaanite did not speak with his mouth and did not walk with his feet, yet he brought rescue to himself and his descendants until the end of all generations. Then someone who actually escorts a person on foot will surely earn much more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the section with a קל וחומר that shows how great the reward for real לויה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man in the story did the smallest possible version of לויה: he only showed the way, without words and without walking along. Real לויה involves walking with the person, so its reward must be even greater. This backs up רבי מאיר's claim that the reward has no limit.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: The זקנים of the עגלה ערופה declare they did not neglect the traveler, meaning food and לויה. רבי מאיר says people may be forced to do לויה, because its reward is endless. This is proven from the man of לוז and a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a kal vachomer?
If this Canaanite,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא דִּיבֵּר בְּפִיו, וְלֹא הָלַךְ בְּרַגְלָיו —
phrases.english: who did not speak with his mouth and did not walk with his feet,
brought rescue to himself and to his descendants
until the end of all generations,
then one who does accompaniment with his feet,
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story in steps 20-21 to reach the conclusion about real לויה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Walking with someone to escort them earns an even greater, unlimited reward than the man of לוז received.

steps.title: How did the man show them the way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how exactly the man of לוז showed the army the entrance to the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he show them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a small detail about the story: how did the man point out the way? This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that the man did not openly lead the army; he only showed them. Now the גמרא wants to know the exact gesture, because it shows how small his act of help really was.

phrases.english: With what did he show them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the army scouts looking for the way into the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story of the man of לוז to clarify a detail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gesture the man used to point out the entrance.

steps.title: Two opinions: with his mouth or with his finger
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says he twisted his mouth toward the entrance; רבי יוחנן says he pointed with his finger.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה says: he twisted his mouth for them. רבי יוחנן says: he showed them with his finger.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in different ways. One says he gestured with his mouth, and the other says he pointed with his finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that he did not speak or walk with them. Either way, his act was tiny. That makes the reward even more striking.

phrases.english: חזקיה said: He twisted his mouth for them,
phrases.notes: He pointed with his lips, without saying a word.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ הֶרְאָה לָהֶם.
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said: He showed them with his finger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a twist of the mouth (חזקיה) or a point of the finger (רבי יוחנן).

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the כנעני pointed with his finger and earned rescue for himself and his descendants forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: Because this כנעני showed them with his finger, he earned rescue for himself and his children until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רבי יוחנן's opinion that the man used his finger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says outright "with his finger," which backs רבי יוחנן. It also stresses the size of the reward: rescue for all generations, for one small motion of a finger.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports him

steps.whatToRemember: Even a tiny act of showing someone the way, just a point of the finger, brought rescue for all generations.

phrases.english: It was taught in line with רבי יוחנן:
Because this Canaanite showed with his finger,
he brought about rescue for himself and his descendants
until the end of all generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports one side of the disagreement in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that he pointed with his finger.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says "he showed with his finger."

steps.title: No escort? Learn Torah on the way
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that someone traveling without a companion should learn Torah, because Torah is called a לויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who walks on the road and has no one to escort him should learn Torah, as it says: "For they are a garland (לוית) of grace for your head, and necklaces for your neck."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new saying about לויה. If no person walks with you, Torah can be your escort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the word לוית, which sounds like לויה. So רבי יהושע בן לוי reads it to mean that Torah itself accompanies and protects a traveler.

keyTerms.meaning: He should busy himself with Torah

phrases.english: רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
One who walks on the road and has no escort,
should busy himself with Torah, as it says:
"For they are a garland of grace for your head,
phrases.notes: משלי 1:9. The word לוית sounds like לויה, escort, and that is the hint.

phrases.english: and necklaces for your neck."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הַמְהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאֵין לוֹ לְוָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לוז story to new teachings about לויה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler without an escort should learn Torah, which acts as his escort.

steps.title: Pharaoh's four steps with אברהם
steps.stepSummary: Because פרעה escorted אברהם four steps, he earned the right to enslave אברהם's descendants for four hundred years.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Because of four steps that פרעה escorted אברהם, as it says "And פרעה commanded men about him," he got to enslave his children for four hundred years, as it says "And they will enslave them and afflict them four hundred years."
steps.whatsHappening: A second saying from רבי יהושע בן לוי shows that even a wicked king got a big reward for a few steps of לויה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four steps match four hundred years. The point is that even a little לויה earns a huge reward, even when the person doing it is פרעה.

keyTerms.meaning: "And so on": the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה פְּסִיעוֹת שֶׁלִּוָּה פַּרְעֹה לְאַבְרָהָם,
phrases.english: Because of four steps that פרעה escorted אברהם,
as it says: "And פרעה commanded men about him, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:20. The rest of the פסוק says they sent him on his way.

phrases.english: he enslaved his children for four hundred years,
phrases.notes: "He" is פרעה and "his children" are אברהם's descendants.

phrases.english: as it says: "And they will enslave them and afflict them
four hundred years."
phrases.notes: בראשית 15:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: בִּשְׁבִיל אַרְבָּעָה פְּסִיעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same אמורא on the power of לויה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A few steps of לויה earn a reward far bigger than the act, even for פרעה.

steps.title: Four אמות of escort protects from harm
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that whoever escorts his friend four אמות in a city will not be harmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who escorts his friend four אמות in the city will not be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical promise: even a short escort of four אמות in town protects the one who does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we saw rewards for לויה on the road. Here רב says that even a tiny escort inside a city counts and brings protection.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of רב:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמְלַוֶּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בָּעִיר —
phrases.english: Anyone who escorts his friend four אמות in the city
is not harmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמְלַוֶּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reward of לויה, now for a short escort in town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Escorting a friend four אמות in a city protects the escort from harm.

steps.title: רבינא's story proves רב's promise
steps.stepSummary: רבינא escorted רבא בר יצחק four אמות in a city, came close to harm, and was saved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא escorted רבא בר יצחק four אמות in the city. Harm came near him, and he was saved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real event that shows רב's promise coming true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Danger really did come close to רבינא, but he was rescued. The story shows that the four אמות of escort protected him.

phrases.english: רבינא escorted רבא בר יצחק
four אמות in the city.
Harm reached him, and he was saved.
phrases.notes: Literally "harm reached his hands": it came close to him, but he escaped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows step 28 coming true in a real event.
steps.raayaObject: רב's promise that a four-אמות escort is not harmed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The event with רבינא and רבא בר יצחק.

steps.title: How far each person must escort
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets distances: a רב escorts a תלמיד to the edge of the city, a friend escorts a friend to the תחום שבת, and a תלמיד escorts a רב with no fixed limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A teacher escorts a student until the edge of the city. A friend escorts a friend until the תחום שבת. A student escorts a teacher with no set measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with clear distances for לויה, depending on who is escorting whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more honor the traveler deserves, the farther you walk with him. A תלמיד owes his רב the most, so there is no fixed limit, and the next step asks what that really means.

keyTerms.meaning: The outskirts of the city, just past the houses
The Shabbos boundary, 2000 אמות from the city

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A teacher, for a student,
escorts him until the outskirts of the city;
a friend, for a friend, until the Shabbos boundary;
a student, for a teacher, there is no set measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rewards of לויה to how far one must go.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Distance of לויה depends on the relationship: רב to תלמיד, the city's edge; friend to friend, the תחום שבת; תלמיד to רב, no fixed limit.

steps.title: How far is "no limit"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far a תלמיד must actually go, since he cannot be expected to walk the whole trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how far?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what "no set measure" means in practice. This short question sets up רב ששת's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "No measure" cannot mean the תלמיד must go the entire journey. So the גמרא wants a real number.

phrases.english: And how far?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the last clause of the ברייתא in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The real distance a תלמיד must escort his רב.

steps.title: רב ששת: up to a פרסה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that a תלמיד escorts his רב up to one פרסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Up to a פרסה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the number: a תלמיד walks with his רב up to one פרסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So "no measure" means a long distance, much more than a friend's escort, but it still has an end. A פרסה is about four מיל.

keyTerms.meaning: A Persian mile, about four מיל

phrases.english: רב ששת said: Up to a פרסה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.

steps.title: A main רב gets three פרסאות
steps.stepSummary: The one-פרסה rule is only for a רב who is not his main teacher; for his main teacher, the תלמיד escorts three פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this about a teacher who is not his main teacher. But his main teacher, he escorts three פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב ששת's answer. One פרסה is for an ordinary teacher; a רב מובהק gets three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא splits the case into two kinds of רב. The one who taught him most of his learning deserves three times the escort.

keyTerms.meaning: His main teacher, from whom he learned most of his knowledge

steps.whatToRemember: Escort distances: רב to תלמיד, the city's edge; friend to friend, the תחום שבת; תלמיד to ordinary רב, one פרסה; תלמיד to רב מובהק, three פרסאות.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא רַבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּבְהָק,
phrases.english: And we only said this about his teacher who is not his main teacher,
but his main teacher, three פרסאות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא רַבּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּבְהָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב ששת's one-פרסה answer to a teacher who is not the main one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A רב מובהק is escorted three פרסאות; any other רב, one פרסה.

steps.title: רב כהנא escorts רב שימי and asks about the palm trees
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא escorts רב שימי בר אשי from פום נהרא to the palm groves of בבל, and there asks him whether the palms really go back to the days of אדם הראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא escorted רב שימי בר אשי from פום נהרא to the palm groves of בבל. When they arrived there, he said to him: Is it true that you say these palm trees of בבל have been here since the years of אדם הראשון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story of לויה in action, and on the walk רב כהנא asks a question. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story first shows a real long escort between חכמים. Then the conversation turns to a question about the ancient palm trees, which will be answered next.

phrases.aramaic: רַב כָּהֲנָא אַלְוְיֵהּ לְרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: רב כהנא escorted רב שימי בר אשי

phrases.aramaic: מִפּוּם נַהֲרָא עַד בֵּי צִינְיָתָא דְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: from פום נהרא to the palm grove of Bavel.
When they arrived there, he said to him:
phrases.notes: רב כהנא is the one asking.

phrases.english: Is it true that you say
that these palm trees of Bavel
have been here since the years of אדם הראשון?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אַלְוְיֵהּ לְרַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a real story of a long לויה, and opens a question that continues in the next step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the palm trees of Bavel really date back to אדם הראשון.

steps.title: רב שימי recalls a puzzling פסוק about an empty land
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי is reminded of a teaching by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. That teaching opens by pointing out that a פסוק in ירמיהו seems to repeat itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You reminded me of something רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said. What does the פסוק mean, 'a land no man passed through and where no person dwelt'? If nobody passed through, where could anyone live? (And if nobody lived there, where would anyone pass?)
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי begins his answer to רב כהנא by quoting a teaching that starts with a question on a פסוק. The answer to that question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says no one passed through and also that no one lived there. If nobody even passed through, then of course nobody lived there, so the second half seems to add nothing. This sets up a new reading of the word אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
But since... (points out that something seems obvious)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב שימי בר אשי, answering רב כהנא's question about the palm trees.

phrases.english: You have reminded me of something
that Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Through a land that no man passed through,
and where no person dwelt"?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 2:6

phrases.english: But since no one passed through it,
where would anyone dwell?
(And since no one dwelt there, where did anyone pass through?)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out these words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַדְכַּרְתַּן מִלְּתָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רב שימי's reply to רב כהנא's question about the palms and אדם הראשון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק add 'no person dwelt there' when 'no one passed through' already covers it?

steps.title: אדם הראשון decided which lands would be settled
steps.stepSummary: The word אדם in the פסוק means אדם הראשון. A land he decreed would be settled became settled, and a land he did not decree for settlement stayed empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: A land that אדם הראשון decreed would be settled was settled. A land he did not decree upon was not settled.
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching solves the puzzle by reading אדם as אדם הראשון himself. This also gives רב כהנא his answer: yes, these places go back to אדם הראשון's decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק is no longer a repeat. It means the land was empty because אדם הראשון never decreed that people would live there. So places like the palm groves of בבל exist as settled land because of his decree.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק reads 'no אדם dwelt there' as 'אדם הראשון never decreed it would be settled.' That is why רב שימי connects it to the palm groves.

phrases.english: Rather:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ שֶׁגָּזַר עָלֶיהָ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְיִשּׁוּב —
phrases.english: A land about which Adam the first man decreed that it be settled
phrases.notes: Here the word אדם in the פסוק is read as Adam himself, not just 'a person.'

phrases.english: was settled;

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ שֶׁלֹּא גָּזַר עָלֶיהָ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן —
phrases.english: a land about which Adam the first man did not decree
was not settled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אֶרֶץ שֶׁגָּזַר עָלֶיהָ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן לְיִשּׁוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question on the פסוק raised in step 35, and so answers רב כהנא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אדם in the פסוק means אדם הראשון: lands settle only where he decreed settlement.

steps.title: How far רב מרדכי escorted רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: Another escorting story: רב מרדכי escorted רב אשי from הגרוניא to בי כיפי. Some say he went as far as בי דורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי escorted רב אשי from הגרוניא until בי כיפי. Some say: until בי דורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more real-life example of a תלמיד escorting his רב on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב כהנא's story, this shows אמוראים actually practicing the escort rules from steps 30 to 33. The two versions just disagree about where the escort ended.

phrases.english: Rav Mordechai escorted Rav Ashi
from Hagronya until Bei Keifei,
and some say: until Bei Dura.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second escorting story, after the story of רב כהנא and רב שימי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אמוראים practiced escorting their teachers over real distances.

steps.title: Not escorting is like spilling blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי מאיר: anyone who does not escort others, or does not let himself be escorted, is like someone who spills blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: Whoever does not escort, or does not let himself be escorted, is as if he spills blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a strong statement about how serious escorting is. The proof follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the sugya gave distances for escorting. Now it says that skipping escort is not a small slip. It is compared to spilling blood, because harm can come to an unescorted traveler.
steps.confusionAlert: This covers both sides. The host must escort, and the traveler must also agree to be escorted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Whoever does not escort, or allow himself to be escorted,
is as if he spills blood,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְלַוֶּה וּמִתְלַוֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from escorting stories to a general statement of how serious escorting is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failing to escort, or refusing to be escorted, is compared to spilling blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for how seriously חז"ל treat the מצוה of לוויה.

steps.title: The proof from אלישע and the bears
steps.stepSummary: Had the people of יריחו escorted אלישע, he would not have set bears on the children. The פסוק shows youths came out and mocked him while he walked alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: For had the people of יריחו escorted אלישע, he would not have set bears on the children. As it says: 'And he went up from there to בית אל, and as he was going up on the way, young lads came out of the city and mocked him and said to him: Go up, baldhead; go up, baldhead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי מאיר's statement from the story of אלישע. Because nobody escorted him, he was mocked, and children ended up dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that lives were lost because of a failure to escort. That is why not escorting is compared to spilling blood. The פסוק shows the youths met אלישע while he was traveling alone.

phrases.english: For had the people of Jericho escorted Elisha,
he would not have set bears upon the children,
as it is stated:
"And he went up from there to Beit El,
and as he was going up on the way,
young lads came out of the city
and mocked him, and said to him:
Go up, baldhead; go up, baldhead."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for רבי מאיר's statement in step 38.
steps.raayaObject: Not escorting is like spilling blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of אלישע and the youths (מלכים ב 2:23). The tragedy happened because nobody escorted him.

steps.title: What the youths meant by 'go up, baldhead'
steps.stepSummary: The youths were not only mocking אלישע's head. They were saying, 'Go away, because you made our place bare.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Go up, for you have made the place bald for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the story in detail, starting with the meaning of the taunt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קרח is read as a play on words. It means 'you made our place bare (הקרחת)', a complaint against אלישע, not just an insult about baldness.

phrases.english: They said to him: Go up (away from here),
for you have made the place bald for us.
phrases.notes: A play on קרח: not 'bald head' but 'you left our place bare.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: עֲלֵה, שֶׁהִקְרַחְתָּ עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַמָּקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the פסוק quoted in step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עלה קרח' means 'leave, for you made our place bare.'

steps.title: Why the double phrase 'young lads'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by calling them both נערים and קטנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'young lads'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the wording of the פסוק. The answers come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two words seem to say the same thing twice. That suggests each word is teaching something about these youths.

phrases.english: What is meant by "young lads"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק, now looking at how it describes the youths.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What do the two words נערים and קטנים each add?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: empty of מצוות and small in faith
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads נערים as 'shaken empty of מצוות' and קטנים as 'small in faith.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: 'Lads' means they were shaken empty of the מצוות. 'Young' means they were of little faith.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers by reading each word as describing the youths' spiritual state, not their age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נערים is linked to מנוערים, meaning shaken out or emptied. קטנים is linked to קטני אמנה, meaning people of small faith. So the words describe their character, not how old they were.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
"Lads" means that they were shaken empty of the מצוות;
phrases.notes: He is reading נערים like מנוערים, shaken out.

phrases.english: "young" means that they were of little faith.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁמְּנוֹעָרִים מִן הַמִּצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נערים means emptied of מצוות, and קטנים means small in faith.

steps.title: A ברייתא: grown youths who acted like children
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that they were already of age (נערים), but they disgraced themselves like little children (קטנים).
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: They were lads, but they made themselves worthless like little children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second explanation of 'young lads' from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי אלעזר, this reading keeps the words about age. נערים means they were old enough to be responsible. קטנים describes how childishly and shamefully they acted. So they were responsible for what they did.

keyTerms.meaning: They disgraced themselves, made themselves worthless

steps.whatToRemember: The two words describe the youths in two ways: by their spiritual state (רבי אלעזר), or as grown youths who acted like children (the ברייתא).

phrases.english: It was taught:
They were lads (already of age),
but they disgraced themselves like little children.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: נְעָרִים הָיוּ, וּבִזְבְּזוּ עַצְמָן כִּקְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 41, different from רבי אלעזר's in step 42.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were old enough to be responsible, but they behaved shamefully like small children.

steps.title: Maybe נערים is just the name of their hometown
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges the earlier explanations of נערים and קטנים. He suggests that נערים may simply mean they came from a place called נעורן, as רבי פדת explained a similar פסוק about a captured girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: maybe they were called נערים after their place. Isn't it written that Aram captured a 'נערה קטנה' from Israel? We found that hard, since how can she be both a young woman and a little girl. רבי פדת answered that it means a little girl from the town of נעורן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on the earlier readings of נערים and קטנים. He offers a simpler idea: נערים could be a place name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 42 and 43 read נערים and קטנים as describing the youths' character or age. רב יוסף points out that the same word pair was already solved elsewhere by treating נערה as 'from נעורן.' If that works there, it could work here too, and the deep readings would not be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, raising a strong challenge
A town's name, which sounds like נערים

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
And perhaps [they were called נערים] after their place?
Isn't it written:
"And Aram went out in raiding bands,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:2

phrases.english: and they took captive from the land of Israel
a young woman, a little one",
and it was difficult for us:
"a young woman" and also "a little one"?
And Rabbi Pedat said:
a little girl who was from Ne'oran!
phrases.notes: So in that פסוק, נערה isn't describing her age. It just tells us her hometown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the readings of נערים and קטנים given in steps 42 and 43
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanations of נערים and קטנים as describing the youths' character or age
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A precedent (רבי פדת on נערה קטנה) shows the same word pair can be solved by treating the word as a place name, so the deeper readings may be unnecessary

steps.title: Here the youths' place is already known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case of the captured girl is different. There the פסוק never says where she came from, but here the youths' place is already stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, her place is not specified. Here, their place is specified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב יוסף's challenge by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading נערה as 'from נעורן' works only when the פסוק gives no other hometown. In our story the youths' place is already given, so נערים cannot be a hometown name. The earlier explanations of נערים and קטנים therefore stand.

phrases.english: There, her place is not specified;
here, their place is specified.
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא connected these youths to יריחו, so we already know where they were from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נערים might be a hometown name, as נערה was for the captured girl
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the youths' place is already stated, נערים cannot be a hometown name. It must describe the youths themselves.
steps.whatToRemember: A word is read as a place name only when the פסוק does not already tell us the place.

steps.title: What did אלישע see before cursing them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the פסוק, that אלישע turned, saw the youths, and cursed them. It asks what exactly he 'saw.'
steps.simpleTranslation: "And he turned behind him and saw them, and cursed them in the name of ה׳." What did he see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the story and asks a question. Several answers will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'saw' seems extra, since the youths were right there. The גמרא takes it to mean that אלישע saw something special that led to the curse.

phrases.english: "And he turned behind him and saw them,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:24

phrases.english: and he cursed them in the name of ה׳."
What did he see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'saw' adds, and what אלישע noticed before cursing them

steps.title: רב: He really looked at them, and a חכם's look can harm
steps.stepSummary: רב says אלישע literally looked at them. He supports this with a ברייתא in which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל teaches that wherever the חכמים set their eyes, death or poverty followed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: he literally saw. As it was taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, any place the חכמים set their eyes upon, there was either death or poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: the 'seeing' itself was the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'saw' means a real, piercing look. The ברייתא shows that a חכם's gaze has power to bring harm, so the look was part of the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Set their eyes upon, stared at

phrases.english: Rav said: he literally saw.
As it was taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Any place upon which the Sages set their eyes —
[there came] either death or poverty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to 'what did he see'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A literal, harmful gaze, supported by the ברייתא that a Sage's gaze brings death or poverty

steps.title: שמואל: They were conceived on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says אלישע saw that all of them had been conceived on יום הכיפורים, when marital relations are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: he saw that all their mothers became pregnant with them on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer: אלישע saw something wrong in how they came into the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, 'saw' means seeing into their background, not a physical stare. Being conceived on a forbidden day showed these youths came from a sinful start.

keyTerms.meaning: The fast day when marital relations are forbidden

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
he saw that all of their mothers became pregnant with them
on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw that they were conceived on יום הכיפורים

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: They wore non-Jewish hairstyles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says אלישע saw they had grown a בלורית, a lock of hair styled the way non-Jews wore it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: he saw that they had a בלורית, like the non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer: אלישע saw that they were copying non-Jewish ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'seeing' is something visible on the outside. Their hairstyle showed that they had cast off Jewish identity.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown lock of hair worn in non-Jewish style

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
he saw that they had grown locks of hair, like the non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw non-Jewish hairstyles on them

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Not even a drop of מצוה in them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אלישע saw that they had not even the smallest trace of a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: he saw that there was not in them even a drop of moisture of a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer: אלישע saw that they were completely empty of מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since they had no merit at all, nothing could protect them from the curse. This answer will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A bit of moisture, the tiniest trace

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
he saw that there was not in them
even a drop of moisture of a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth answer to the same question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He saw that they had no מצוות at all

steps.title: But maybe their descendants would have done מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's answer. Even if the youths had no מצוות, perhaps their future children would, so why curse them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps among their descendants there would have been [מצוות]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no merit yourself may not be enough reason to destroy someone. If good people might come from them, that should have saved them.

phrases.english: But perhaps among their descendants there would have been [מצוות]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason for the curse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lacking מצוות now does not justify the curse if their descendants might do מצוות

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: No מצוות in their descendants forever
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that אלישע saw there would be no מצוות in them or in any of their descendants until the end of all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: not in them and not in their descendants, until the end of all generations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge on רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע saw not only the youths but their entire future line. Since no merit would ever come from them, the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the end of all generations

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Not in them and not in their descendants
until the end of all generations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לֹא בָּם וְלֹא בְּזַרְעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their descendants might have had מצוות, which would have protected them
steps.terutzMaskana: אלישע saw that no מצוות would ever come from them or their descendants
steps.whatToRemember: Four views of what אלישע 'saw': רב says a harmful stare, שמואל says conception on יום הכיפורים, רבי יצחק נפחא says non-Jewish hairstyles, and רבי יוחנן says no מצוות at all. רבי אלעזר adds that this was true of their descendants forever.

steps.title: The two bears come out of the forest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the פסוק: two she-bears came out of the forest and tore apart forty-two children.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And two she-bears came out of the forest and tore apart forty-two children from them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the story. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is explained yet. The quote opens the next part of the story, which the גמרא will now examine.

phrases.english: "And two she-bears came out of the forest
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 2:24

phrases.english: and tore apart from them
forty-two children",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next part of the פסוק after the curse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the פסוק about the bears as the base text for the next discussion
